extracted.intended_audience: journalism and English composition educators, researchers, and curriculum planners
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based research assessing journalism students' perceptions of freshman English composition as preparation for news writing, and identifying which course/incoming factors best predict success in introductory journalism. Compares skills stressed by composition vs journalism across two universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How valuable was the writing instruction you received in your first freshman English composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking students to rate the overall value of their first freshman composition course (1 = none at all; 2 = a little; 3 = a moderate amount; 4 = quite a bit; 5 = very much).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analysis responses 1-3 were combined as 'low' and 4-5 as 'high'. Used to compare by institution, grade, ACT, major, and sex; reported means and percent 'quite a bit'/'very much'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How useful for the work world was the writing instruction you received in your first freshman composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking perceived usefulness of freshman composition for professional/work writing (same 1-5 scale as above).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses dichotomized (1-3 low, 4-5 high). Percentages, means, and cross-tabulations by institution and independent variables reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: How useful for your other academic writing (other than journalism) was the writing instruction you received in your first freshman composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking perceived usefulness of freshman composition for non-journalism academic writing (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses dichotomized into low/high; compared across institutions and independent variables; reported mean and percent 'quite a bit'/'very much'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How useful for your journalistic writing was the writing instruction you received in your first freshman composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking perceived usefulness of freshman composition specifically for journalistic writing (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses combined 1-3 low, 4-5 high. Used to assess whether composition prepares students for journalism; cross-tabulated with grades, ACT, major, sex, institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much grammar instruction did you receive in your first freshman composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking students to rate amount of grammar instruction received in freshman composition (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percent responding 'quite a bit'/'very much' and mean; compared with perceived strictness in grading and with high-school grammar instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: How much grammar instruction did you receive in your high school English classes (10th through 12th grades)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking about prior grammar instruction received in high school (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an independent variable (extent of previous grammar instruction) in predicting success in composition and journalism; reported percent 'quite a bit'/'very much'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How strict was the English instructor in your first freshman composition course in grading your writing for grammar mistakes?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item rating instructor strictness in grading grammar in freshman composition (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as part of 'previous grammar and spelling instruction' variable; analyzed as predictor of student success.

rubrics_metrics.name: How strict was the English instructor in your first freshman composition course in grading your writing for spelling mistakes?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item rating instructor strictness in grading spelling in freshman composition (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzed similarly to grammar-grading strictness; reported percent 'quite a bit'/'very much'.

rubrics_metrics.name: How well did you like your first freshman composition course?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking students how much they liked the freshman composition course (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percent liking the course and mean; compared across institutions and other variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: How well did you like the writing portions of your introductory journalism writing courses?
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item about students' liking of the writing portions of their introductory journalism courses (1-5 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percent 'quite a bit'/'very much' and mean; used to contrast student attitudes toward journalism vs composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of time devoted to writing in freshman composition compared to literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking whether students thought too little time was devoted to writing versus literature in freshman composition (responses include 'not enough').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percent indicating 'not enough' and mean; used to discuss whether composition is 'contentless' or literature-heavy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of time devoted to writing in introductory journalism course compared to non-writing topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey item asking whether journalism courses devote sufficient time to writing versus non-writing topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported percent saying 'not enough' and mean; used to compare emphasis on writing in journalism vs composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing concisely
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills identified from course objectives; students rated how well composition and journalism courses taught writing 'concisely'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on same Likert scale, means computed for each course and institution, ranks produced; differences and Pearson r/Spearman rho correlations reported; journalism generally rated higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; student ratings of how well composition and journalism taught writing 'precisely'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means, ranks, and differences reported by institution; used in correlations comparing the two courses' skill emphases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; ratings for how well courses taught writing 'clearly'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compared between composition and journalism with means, ranks, and inter-course correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organized (writing organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; students rated course emphasis on producing organized writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among top-rated skills in some comparisons; means and ranks reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar (use of correct grammar)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; student ratings of emphasis on correct grammar in composition and journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported means and ranks; finding noted that journalism courses at two institutions were most alike for teaching grammar while composition courses varied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling (use of correct spelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; ratings of how well courses taught correct spelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means/ranks reported; commonly among top skills for journalism in this study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; students rated how well courses taught writing with audience awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare similarity between courses; one of the more similar skills between composition and journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing interestingly
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; ratings of instruction in creating interesting writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as part of 'reflective skills' cluster; means and ranks reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing creatively
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; students rated emphasis on creativity in writing instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as a 'reflective' skill; composition often rated higher than journalism on creativity in this study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing in detail
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; ratings for teaching detail in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means and ranks reported; part of reflective skills group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using one's own opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: One of 11 skills; rated how much courses encouraged use of personal opinion in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified as a reflective skill; composition tended to emphasize opinions more than journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical skills vs. reflective skills (definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational definitions used in hypotheses: Practical skills = writing concisely, precisely, clearly, with good organization, using good grammar, proper spelling, and writing for one's audience. Reflective skills = writing interestingly, creatively, in detail, and using one's own opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to frame Hypothesis 2 that journalism teaches practical skills while freshman composition teaches reflective skills; guided grouping of the 11 skills during analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictor variables for success in introductory journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent variables examined as predictors: sex, print journalism major status, English ACT score, composite ACT score, freshman composition grade, and extent of previous grammar and spelling instruction (including perceived strictness of grading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grades dichotomized as 'A' vs 'non-A'; ACT cutoffs classified as high (23 or above) vs low (22 and below). Hypothesis proposed that freshman composition grade would be the best predictor; analysis found English ACT, composite ACT, and gender to be better predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade classification: A vs non-A
rubrics_metrics.description: Students' letter grades in freshman composition and introductory journalism were categorized as 'A' or 'non-A' for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in chi-square tests and cross-tabulations to identify relationships between grades and perceptions/usefulness ratings and to test hypotheses about predictors of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACT score classification: high vs low
rubrics_metrics.description: English ACT and composite ACT scores were categorized as high (23 or above) or low (22 and below) for analytical comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as predictors in cross-tabulations and chi-square tests; significance reported for relationships with course grades and perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likert-to-dichotomy scoring convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic convention: For almost all survey items the 1-5 scale was collapsed so that responses 1-3 = low and 4-5 = high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dichotomization was used consistently throughout analyses, tables, and reported chi-square/Cramer's V statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional accreditation/status as a comparative factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison variable: South Dakota State (ACEJMC accredited) vs Southwest Missouri State (not accredited, offers only a journalism minor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test Hypothesis 4 that perceptions would differ by institution; analyses control for institution in many tables and report institution-specific differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching approach: process writing vs other methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive/evaluative criterion about instructional method: many composition programs use 'process writing'; journalism instruction may use process or a more product/practical approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed as explanatory background affecting whether composition prepares students for journalism; not directly scored but presented as a contextual criterion for curriculum design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and simple writing as a criterion of good journalistic writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative standard from literature: 'good journalistic writing is clear and simple' (Mencher) and journalism techniques provide clarity and precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in literature review to justify why journalism instruction may better prepare students for workplace writing; cited studies where English graders preferred wordy prose over clear writing.
